key_insight: CAT-CKD improves skin lesion classification across heterogeneous datasets by combining lightweight adapter training with consensus knowledge distillation.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more consistent melanoma-versus-benign-nevus classification across imaging sources without requiring source-data access during adaptation.
method: Train lightweight ConvPass adapters in a frozen vision transformer using supervised contrastive learning to align source-domain features.
Combine predictions from source-specific models into a consensus supervisory signal.
Adapt a student model on unlabeled target images using KL-divergence distillation.
evidence_signal: Across five public skin lesion datasets, CAT-CKD achieved an average AUROC of 86.1%, outperforming evaluated MSFDA methods with 4.3 million trainable parameters.
watch_item: Public-dataset performance does not establish clinical readiness; prospective validation and assessment across patient subgroups remain important.
paper_title: Contrastive Adapter Training and Consensus Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Skin Cancer Diagnosis
